subject: anatomy
title: Neural Induction and Neural Crest Migration

steps.tx: Neurulation is the embryonic process transforming midline ectoderm into the neural tube. Induced by chordin, noggin, and follistatin secreted by the notochord, the overlying ectoderm thickens to form the slipper-shaped **neural plate** during the third gestational week. This specialized neuroectoderm gives origin to the brain and spinal cord.
steps.say: Neurulation converts surface ectoderm into the neural tube. Stimulated by morphogens from the notochord, overlying ectoderm thickens into the slipper-like neural plate during week three. This neuroectoderm generates the entire central nervous system.

vis.alt: Neural plate, neural groove, neural folds, and neural tube closure
vis.caption: Neurulation and neural tube closure along the dorsal midline. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: As the lateral margins of the neural plate elevate, they produce paired longitudinal neural folds flanking a central depressed neural groove. The elevated crests of the folds converge toward the midline, where the **neural tube** fuses. Closure begins in the cervical region at the level of the fifth somite and zips cranially and caudally.
steps.say: The edges of the neural plate elevate to form paired neural folds flanking a central neural groove. The converging crests meet in the midline to form the neural tube. Fusion initiates in the cervical region and zips both headward and tailward.

steps.tx: The cranial and caudal extremities of the neural tube communicate temporarily with the amniotic cavity via neuropores. The **anterior neuropore** closes reliably on day twenty-five (at the eighteen to twenty somite stage). Failure of anterior neuropore closure prevents calvarial and cerebral development, resulting in lethal anencephaly.
steps.say: Open ends of the neural tube communicate with amniotic fluid through neuropores. The anterior neuropore seals on day twenty-five. Failure of anterior closure halts brain and skull vault development, producing lethal anencephaly.

steps.tx: The **posterior neuropore** closes three days later on gestational day twenty-eight (at the twenty-five somite stage). Failure of posterior neuropore closure causes spina bifida, ranging from occult vertebral defects to open myelomeningocele with neurological paralysis. Periconceptional maternal supplementation with folic acid dramatically reduces neural tube defect rates by seventy percent.
steps.say: The posterior neuropore seals on day twenty-eight. Defective closure causes spina bifida, ranging from minor vertebral gaps to myelomeningocele with lower-limb paralysis. Maternal periconceptional folic acid supplementation prevents over seventy percent of these anomalies.

vis.alt: Folic acid supplementation mechanism in neural tube closure
vis.caption: Folic acid prevention of neural tube defects and closed neuropores. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: During neural fold elevation, a specialized population of cells along the fold crest undergoes epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition and detaches, designated **neural crest** cells. Often termed the fourth germ layer, these multipotent migratory cells journey extensively along defined pathways throughout the embryo, differentiating into diverse tissue types.
steps.say: As neural folds elevate, a specialized population at the fold crest detaches, forming neural crest cells. Referred to as the fourth germ layer, these migratory cells journey along embryonic pathways to differentiate into diverse nervous, endocrine, and skeletal structures.

steps.tx: Trunk neural crest cells migrate along two main pathways: a dorsolateral route under the ectoderm to form **melanocytes** in the skin, and a ventral route through anterior sclerotomes. The ventral stream differentiates into dorsal root sensory ganglia, sympathetic chain ganglia, parasympathetic enteric plexuses of Meissner and Auerbach, and chromaffin cells of the adrenal medulla.
steps.say: Trunk neural crest cells follow two routes: a superficial path under the ectoderm to become cutaneous melanocytes, and a deep ventral path through somites. The ventral stream yields sensory ganglia, sympathetic chains, enteric plexuses, and adrenal chromaffin cells.

steps.tx: In the head and neck, cranial neural crest cells form the ectomesenchyme that builds the branchial arches, the frontonasal process, the bones of the face, and the aorticopulmonary septum. Defective migration of cranial neural crest cells into the outflow tract of the heart causes conotruncal heart defects, including **tetralogy of Fallot** and persistent truncus arteriosus.
steps.say: In the head, cranial crest cells form ectomesenchyme constructing facial bones, branchial arches, and the aorticopulmonary septum. Defective crest migration into the cardiac outflow tract leads to conotruncal defects like tetralogy of Fallot and persistent truncus arteriosus.

steps.tx: Failure of vagal neural crest cells to migrate into the distal colonic wall results in congenital absence of myenteric Auerbach and submucosal Meissner plexuses, causing **Hirschsprung disease**. The aganglionic bowel segment undergoes chronic tonic contraction, creating functional bowel obstruction and massive proximal megacolon in neonates.
steps.say: Failure of neural crest cells to colonize the distal colon eliminates myenteric and submucosal plexuses, causing Hirschsprung disease. The aganglionic segment remains spastically contracted, creating distal bowel obstruction and marked proximal megacolon.
